auditPolicy.activationRule: A city is ready only when every visible plate has a unique human place name and every merge is exact-ID, connected and semantically coherent.
auditPolicy.suffixRule: Strip and dissolve an Arabic suffix only when every cell in the family shares the same base label and the official polygons form a connected graph.
auditPolicy.technicalRule: A directional, generic, land-use or station label may be retained only by an exact-ID accept operation citing IGN/INSEE plus a dated Guide Alpha editorial review. Opaque inventories require exact-ID human renames supported by IGN named points strictly contained in each source polygon; nearest-point assignment is forbidden.
auditPolicy.geometryAdjacency: At least two shared boundary vertices at seven decimal places; every grouped family must form one connected graph.
auditPolicy.strictToponymRule: For technical H inventories, each rename is assigned only when every cited IGN named-point coordinate is strictly inside the exact official IRIS polygon. No nearest-point assignment is permitted.

anomalies.detail: All twelve IRIS are technical Cambrai-number cells. The official City of Cambrai page names Saint-Roch, Victor Hugo/Amérique, Saint-Druon, Martin-Martine, Cantimpré/Port fluvial and Vieux Cambrai. IGN official named points anchor Cantimpré→591220101, Saint-Roch→591220102, Victor Hugo→591220103, Amérique→591220104, Martin-Martine→591220105, Vieux Cambrai→591220108 and Saint-Druon→591220114, but no official polygon crosswalk covers all twelve cells. Collapsing the connected family to one city-wide plate would violate Guide Alpha; no operation is approved. Resolution: All twelve technical Cambrai-number cells receive unique exact-ID human labels from IGN named points strictly contained in their own IRIS, with the official City of Cambrai neighbourhood publication as municipal context.
